If that carries over, it supports Brissett’s floor but leans the offense toward short-area volume rather than deep-shot ceiling. [3, 7]

- **Arizona red-zone offense** — The Cardinals were only 2-for-5 in the red zone last week. That keeps touchdown upside a little less secure than the yardage output suggests, so Brissett and the skill players may need efficiency rather than pure scoring volume to smash Week 2 projections. [6]

- **Nick Rallis (DC)** — Arizona used Cover 6 on 42.9% of snaps in Week 1, the highest rate in the league. If that zone-heavy approach sticks, it matters most for slowing Seattle’s passing game and modestly helping ARI DST expectations, though it’s more of an opponent-side note than a Cardinals skill-player boost.
